insights.insight: $4.6M in cryptographically verified purchase GMV across 96,434 receipts — deterministic proof of transaction, not modeled inference. At ~$13,700/day structural pace, this corpus is compounding without a visible acceleration event.

The industry pays $5+ CPM to infer purchase intent from behavioral signals; a confirmed receipt eliminates that inference entirely. The gap between 'visited a recipe site' and 'bought groceries, here's the receipt' is the addressable value proposition for cookieless targeting.

Grocery-supermarkets and restaurants-dining account for the majority of 14-day receipt volume, with Walmart at 333 receipts — more than double the next brand. Retail-department-stores matches grocery on implied GMV-per-receipt (~$45.67 vs ~$45.63), signaling basket size parity worth noting for mid-funnel campaign planning.

7-Eleven crossed the visibility threshold on Oct 27 — the first new brand addition in 40+ consecutive snapshots spanning Oct 16 through Oct 26. A 10-day brand-list freeze followed by a c-store entry suggests either a new retail category opening or a single large-account onboarding, not broad convenience-channel penetration yet.

The 7-day window has twice approached but not cleared $100K — peaking at $99,116 before compressing sharply as high-volume days roll off. The ceiling is a pacing artifact, not a demand signal, but it marks the current throughput boundary any brand audience-activation plan should be sized against.

Coverage holds at 20 metro areas with no confirmed structural expansion since Oct 24; a transient 21-metro reading was flagged as an endpoint artifact and reverted. Brands planning geo-targeted activations should treat the current 20-CBSA footprint as the reliable planning boundary until a confirmed structural addition is recorded.
